Labels for an imaginary house museum

Blee Old House Museum is credited to @ajayblee in the historical inventory (page 13). This is a new Reading Shelf exercise inspired by that idea. The objects below are fictional; they are not a collection attributed to Blee Old House Museum. No museum venue is built here.

Choose an object card. Say or write a short label with three parts:

  1. What you can observe. Use a detail from the card.
  2. What might explain it. Use “could” or “might” to show you’re making a guess.
  3. What would help you check. Name another clue or ask a question.

A key with a tied label

A metal key has three teeth. A thread fastens a blank paper label to its loop.

Read one possible label for the key

A blank label is tied to the key. Someone might have planned to write which lock it opens. A dated key list with drawings of the keys could help check that.

A stool with a smooth edge

One edge of a wooden stool is smooth. The opposite edge is rougher. The stool has four legs.

Read one possible label for the stool

One edge is smoother than the other. It might have worn down where people often held it, or someone might have sanded it. A repair note might tell us whether the edge was sanded.

A cup with two colors of thread

A small cup holds short pieces of red and white thread. There is no needle in the cup.

Read one possible label for the cup

The cup holds pieces of thread. It could have held scraps from mending. A sewing box with matching threads would be another clue, but would not tell us who used it.

Read your label aloud. Can someone tell which sentence is an observation and which is a guess? Try changing the guess while keeping the observation the same.
